cues.zh: Chris Anderson：你算得上是数学神童。
cues.en: Chris Anderson: You were something of a mathematical phenom.

cues.zh: 你年纪轻轻就在哈佛和MIT教过书。
cues.en: You had already taught at Harvard and MIT at a young age.

cues.zh: 后来NSA找上了你。
cues.en: And then the NSA came calling.

cues.zh: 那是怎么回事？
cues.en: What was that about?

cues.zh: Jim Simons：嗯，NSA——就是国家安全局——
cues.en: Jim Simons: Well the NSA -- that's the National Security Agency --

cues.zh: 他们倒不是直接找上门来。
cues.en: they didn't exactly come calling.

cues.zh: 他们在普林斯顿有个行动点，雇数学家
cues.en: They had an operation at Princeton, where they hired mathematicians

cues.zh: 去破解密码之类的东西。
cues.en: to attack secret codes and stuff like that.

cues.zh: 我知道那地方存在。
cues.en: And I knew that existed.

cues.zh: 他们的政策很好，
cues.en: And they had a very good policy,

cues.zh: 因为你可以一半时间做自己的数学研究，
cues.en: because you could do half your time at your own mathematics,

cues.zh: 至少一半时间做他们的活儿。
cues.en: and at least half your time working on their stuff.

cues.zh: 而且报酬很高。
cues.en: And they paid a lot.

cues.zh: 所以那诱惑无法抗拒。
cues.en: So that was an irresistible pull.

cues.zh: 于是我就去了。
cues.en: So, I went there.

cues.zh: CA：你是个密码破译者。
cues.en: CA: You were a code-cracker.

cues.zh: JS：没错。
cues.en: JS: I was.

cues.zh: CA：直到你被解雇。
cues.en: CA: Until you got fired.

cues.zh: JS：嗯，我确实被解雇了。是的。
cues.en: JS: Well, I did get fired. Yes.

cues.zh: CA：怎么会呢？
cues.en: CA: How come?

cues.zh: JS：嗯，怎么会呢？
cues.en: JS: Well, how come?

cues.zh: 我被解雇了，因为，嗯，当时正值越南战争，
cues.en: I got fired because, well, the Vietnam War was on,

cues.zh: 而我所在机构的最高老板是这场战争的大力支持者，
cues.en: and the boss of bosses in my organization was a big fan of the war

cues.zh: 还在《纽约时报》上发表了一篇文章，是杂志版的封面故事，
cues.en: and wrote a New York Times article, a magazine section cover story,

cues.zh: 讲我们如何在越南取胜。
cues.en: about how we would win in Vietnam.

cues.zh: 我不喜欢那场战争，我觉得它很愚蠢。
cues.en: And I didn't like that war, I thought it was stupid.

cues.zh: 于是我给《时报》写了封信，他们发表了，
cues.en: And I wrote a letter to the Times, which they published,

cues.zh: 信中说，并非所有为 Maxwell Taylor 工作的人
cues.en: saying not everyone who works for Maxwell Taylor,

cues.zh: ——如果有人还记得这个名字——都认同他的观点。
cues.en: if anyone remembers that name, agrees with his views.

cues.zh: 我表达了自己的看法……
cues.en: And I gave my own views ...

cues.zh: CA：哦，好的。我能理解那会——
cues.en: CA: Oh, OK. I can see that would --

cues.zh: JS：……这些看法与 Taylor 将军的不同。
cues.en: JS: ... which were different from General Taylor's.

cues.zh: 但最后，没人说什么。
cues.en: But in the end, nobody said anything.

cues.zh: 不过后来，我当时29岁，有个年轻人过来
cues.en: But then, I was 29 years old at this time, and some kid came around

cues.zh: 说他是《新闻周刊》杂志的特约记者，
cues.en: and said he was a stringer from Newsweek magazine

cues.zh: 想采访我，问我对自己的观点采取了什么行动。
cues.en: and he wanted to interview me and ask what I was doing about my views.

cues.zh: 我跟他说：“我现在主要研究数学，
cues.en: And I told him, "I'm doing mostly mathematics now,

cues.zh: 等战争结束，我再主要做他们那摊事。”
cues.en: and when the war is over, then I'll do mostly their stuff."

cues.zh: 然后我做了那天唯一一件明智的事——
cues.en: Then I did the only intelligent thing I'd done that day --

cues.zh: 我告诉我的本地老板，我接受了那个采访。
cues.en: I told my local boss that I gave that interview.

cues.zh: 他说：“你都说了什么？”
cues.en: And he said, "What'd you say?"

cues.zh: 我就把我说的话告诉了他。
cues.en: And I told him what I said.

cues.zh: 然后他说：“我得给 Taylor 打个电话。”
cues.en: And then he said, "I've got to call Taylor."

cues.zh: 他打给了 Taylor，花了 10 分钟。
cues.en: He called Taylor; that took 10 minutes.

cues.zh: 五分钟后我就被解雇了。
cues.en: I was fired five minutes after that.

cues.zh: CA：好。
cues.en: CA: OK.

cues.zh: JS：但也不算坏事。
cues.en: JS: But it wasn't bad.

cues.zh: CA：不算坏事，因为你后来去了 Stony Brook
cues.en: CA: It wasn't bad, because you went on to Stony Brook

cues.zh: 数学事业更上一层楼。
cues.en: and stepped up your mathematical career.

cues.zh: 你开始和这位先生合作。
cues.en: You started working with this man here.

cues.zh: 这是谁？
cues.en: Who is this?

cues.zh: JS：哦，[陈省身] Chern。
cues.en: JS: Oh, [Shiing-Shen] Chern.

cues.zh: Chern 是本世纪最伟大的数学家之一。
cues.en: Chern was one of the great mathematicians of the century.

cues.zh: 我在 Berkeley 读研究生时就认识他了。
cues.en: I had known him when I was a graduate student at Berkeley.

cues.zh: 我有些想法，
cues.en: And I had some ideas,

cues.zh: 我拿给他看，他很喜欢。
cues.en: and I brought them to him and he liked them.

cues.zh: 我们一起做了这项工作，你们在上面很容易看到。
cues.en: Together, we did this work which you can easily see up there.

cues.zh: 就是这个。
cues.en: There it is.

cues.zh: CA：这让你们共同发表了一篇著名论文。
cues.en: CA: It led to you publishing a famous paper together.

cues.zh: 你能解释一下那项工作是什么吗？
cues.en: Can you explain at all what that work was?

cues.zh: JS：不能。
cues.en: JS: No.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: JS：我是说，我可以给某些人解释。
cues.en: JS: I mean, I could explain it to somebody.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: CA：那解释一下这个怎么样？
cues.en: CA: How about explaining this?

cues.zh: JS：但没多少人。没多少人能懂。
cues.en: JS: But not many. Not many people.

cues.zh: CA：我记得你告诉过我，那和球面有关，
cues.en: CA: I think you told me it had something to do with spheres,

cues.zh: 那我们就从这里开始吧。
cues.en: so let's start here.

cues.zh: JS：嗯，确实有关，但关于那项工作我要说——
cues.en: JS: Well, it did, but I'll say about that work --

cues.zh: 它确实和那个有关，但在我们谈到那之前——
cues.en: it did have something to do with that, but before we get to that --

cues.zh: 那项工作是很好的数学。
cues.en: that work was good mathematics.

cues.zh: 我对它非常满意；Chern也是。
cues.en: I was very happy with it; so was Chern.

cues.zh: 它甚至开创了一个小分支领域，现在正蓬勃发展。
cues.en: It even started a little sub-field that's now flourishing.

cues.zh: 但更有趣的是，它恰好适用于物理学，
cues.en: But, more interestingly, it happened to apply to physics,

cues.zh: 一些我们一无所知的东西——至少我对物理学一无所知，
cues.en: something we knew nothing about -- at least I knew nothing about physics,

cues.zh: 而且我觉得Chern也懂得不多。
cues.en: and I don't think Chern knew a heck of a lot.

cues.zh: 大约在论文发表 10 年后，
cues.en: And about 10 years after the paper came out,

cues.zh: 普林斯顿一位叫 Ed Witten 的人开始把它用到弦论上
cues.en: a guy named Ed Witten in Princeton started applying it to string theory

cues.zh: 而俄罗斯那边的人开始把它用到所谓的“凝聚态”上。
cues.en: and people in Russia started applying it to what's called "condensed matter."

cues.zh: 今天，那些被称为 Chern-Simons 不变量的东西
cues.en: Today, those things in there called Chern-Simons invariants

cues.zh: 已经传遍了物理学的许多领域。
cues.en: have spread through a lot of physics.

cues.zh: 这太惊人了。
cues.en: And it was amazing.

cues.zh: 我们当时完全不懂物理。
cues.en: We didn't know any physics.

cues.zh: 我从没想过它会被应用到物理学上。
cues.en: It never occurred to me that it would be applied to physics.

cues.zh: 但数学就是这样——你永远不知道它会走向哪里。
cues.en: But that's the thing about mathematics -- you never know where it's going to go.

cues.zh: CA：这太不可思议了。
cues.en: CA: This is so incredible.

cues.zh: 我们一直在讨论进化如何塑造人类心智
cues.en: So, we've been talking about how evolution shapes human minds

cues.zh: 而心智未必能感知真相。
cues.en: that may or may not perceive the truth.

cues.zh: 不知怎么的，你提出了一个数学理论，
cues.en: Somehow, you come up with a mathematical theory,

cues.zh: 完全不懂物理，
cues.en: not knowing any physics,

cues.zh: 二十年后却发现它被应用
cues.en: discover two decades later that it's being applied

cues.zh: 去深刻地描述真实的物理世界。
cues.en: to profoundly describe the actual physical world.

cues.zh: 这怎么可能发生？
cues.en: How can that happen?

cues.zh: JS：天知道。
cues.en: JS: God knows.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: 但有一位著名的物理学家叫 [Eugene] Wigner，
cues.en: But there's a famous physicist named [Eugene] Wigner,

cues.zh: 他写过一篇关于数学那不可理喻的有效性的文章。
cues.en: and he wrote an essay on the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics.

cues.zh: 不知怎么的，这门植根于现实世界的数学
cues.en: Somehow, this mathematics, which is rooted in the real world

cues.zh: 在某种意义上——我们学着数数、测量，人人都会这么做——
cues.en: in some sense -- we learn to count, measure, everyone would do that --

cues.zh: 然后它就自己蓬勃发展起来了。
cues.en: and then it flourishes on its own.

cues.zh: 但它常常又回来拯救局面。
cues.en: But so often it comes back to save the day.

cues.zh: 广义相对论就是一个例子。
cues.en: General relativity is an example.

cues.zh: [Hermann] Minkowski 有了这套几何，而 Einstein 意识到，
cues.en: [Hermann] Minkowski had this geometry, and Einstein realized,

cues.zh: “嘿！这正是我能用来构建广义相对论的东西。”
cues.en: "Hey! It's the very thing in which I can cast general relativity."

cues.zh: 所以，你永远说不准。这是个谜。
cues.en: So, you never know. It is a mystery.

cues.zh: 这是个谜。
cues.en: It is a mystery.

cues.zh: CA：那么，这里有一个数学上的巧思。
cues.en: CA: So, here's a mathematical piece of ingenuity.

cues.zh: 给我们讲讲这个。
cues.en: Tell us about this.

cues.zh: JS：嗯，那是个球——是个球体，周围有一圈晶格——
cues.en: JS: Well, that's a ball -- it's a sphere, and it has a lattice around it --

cues.zh: 你知道，就是那些方块。
cues.en: you know, those squares.

cues.zh: 我要展示的内容，最早是由[Leonhard] Euler观察到的，
cues.en: What I'm going to show here was originally observed by [Leonhard] Euler,

cues.zh: 这位伟大的数学家，在18世纪。
cues.en: the great mathematician, in the 1700s.

cues.zh: 它逐渐发展成为数学中一个非常重要的领域：
cues.en: And it gradually grew to be a very important field in mathematics:

cues.zh: 代数拓扑、几何。
cues.en: algebraic topology, geometry.

cues.zh: 上面那篇论文就源于此。
cues.en: That paper up there had its roots in this.

cues.zh: 那么，就是这个东西：
cues.en: So, here's this thing:

cues.zh: 它有8个顶点、12条边、6个面。
cues.en: it has eight vertices, 12 edges, six faces.

cues.zh: 如果你看这个差值——顶点减边加面——
cues.en: And if you look at the difference -- vertices minus edges plus faces --

cues.zh: 你会得到2。
cues.en: you get two.

cues.zh: 好，就是2。这是个好数字。
cues.en: OK, well, two. That's a good number.

cues.zh: 这是另一种做法——这些是覆盖用的三角形——
cues.en: Here's a different way of doing it -- these are triangles covering --

cues.zh: 这个有12个顶点和30条边
cues.en: this has 12 vertices and 30 edges

cues.zh: 以及20个面，20块瓦片。
cues.en: and 20 faces, 20 tiles.

cues.zh: 顶点减边加面仍然等于2。
cues.en: And vertices minus edges plus faces still equals two.

cues.zh: 事实上，你可以用任何方式来做——
cues.en: And in fact, you could do this any which way --

cues.zh: 用各种多边形和三角形覆盖这个东西
cues.en: cover this thing with all kinds of polygons and triangles

cues.zh: 把它们混在一起。
cues.en: and mix them up.

cues.zh: 顶点数减边数加面数，结果得二。
cues.en: And you take vertices minus edges plus faces -- you'll get two.

cues.zh: 再看一个不同的形状。
cues.en: Here's a different shape.

cues.zh: 这是一个环面，也就是甜甜圈的表面：16个顶点
cues.en: This is a torus, or the surface of a doughnut: 16 vertices

cues.zh: 被这些矩形覆盖，32条边，16个面。
cues.en: covered by these rectangles, 32 edges, 16 faces.

cues.zh: 顶点数减边数，结果为零。
cues.en: Vertices minus edges comes out to be zero.

cues.zh: 它永远都会得零。
cues.en: It'll always come out to zero.

cues.zh: 每当你用正方形或三角形覆盖一个环面
cues.en: Every time you cover a torus with squares or triangles

cues.zh: 或者用类似的东西，结果都是零。
cues.en: or anything like that, you're going to get zero.

cues.zh: 这就叫欧拉示性数。
cues.en: So, this is called the Euler characteristic.

cues.zh: 它是一种所谓的拓扑不变量。
cues.en: And it's what's called a topological invariant.

cues.zh: 这相当了不起。
cues.en: It's pretty amazing.

cues.zh: 无论你怎么做，答案总是一样的。
cues.en: No matter how you do it, you're always get the same answer.

cues.zh: 这就是18世纪中期最初的推动力，
cues.en: So that was the first sort of thrust, from the mid-1700s,

cues.zh: 开启了一门现在叫做代数拓扑的学科。
cues.en: into a subject which is now called algebraic topology.

cues.zh: CA：而你自己的工作借鉴了这样的想法，把它推进
cues.en: CA: And your own work took an idea like this and moved it

cues.zh: 到高维理论中，
cues.en: into higher-dimensional theory,

cues.zh: 高维对象，并发现了新的不变性？
cues.en: higher-dimensional objects, and found new invariances?

cues.zh: JS：是的。其实当时已经有高维不变量了：
cues.en: JS: Yes. Well, there were already higher-dimensional invariants:

cues.zh: 庞特里亚金类——其实还有陈类。
cues.en: Pontryagin classes -- actually, there were Chern classes.

cues.zh: 这类不变量有一大堆。
cues.en: There were a bunch of these types of invariants.

cues.zh: 我当时正努力研究其中一种，
cues.en: I was struggling to work on one of them

cues.zh: 想用组合的方式给它建模，
cues.en: and model it sort of combinatorially,

cues.zh: 而不是用通常的做法，
cues.en: instead of the way it was typically done,

cues.zh: 这就引出了这项工作，我们由此发现了一些新东西。
cues.en: and that led to this work and we uncovered some new things.

cues.zh: 但要不是欧拉先生——
cues.en: But if it wasn't for Mr. Euler --

cues.zh: 他写了将近70卷数学著作，
cues.en: who wrote almost 70 volumes of mathematics

cues.zh: 还有13个孩子，
cues.en: and had 13 children,

cues.zh: 据说他写作时还会把孩子抱在膝上逗弄——
cues.en: who he apparently would dandle on his knee while he was writing --

cues.zh: 要不是欧拉先生，也许就不会有这些不变量。
cues.en: if it wasn't for Mr. Euler, there wouldn't perhaps be these invariants.

cues.zh: CA：好，这至少让我们领略了一下那颗非凡头脑的风采。
cues.en: CA: OK, so that's at least given us a flavor of that amazing mind in there.

cues.zh: 我们来聊聊文艺复兴。
cues.en: Let's talk about Renaissance.

cues.zh: 因为你带着那颗非凡的头脑，先是在NSA做破译工作，
cues.en: Because you took that amazing mind and having been a code-cracker at the NSA,

cues.zh: 然后又开始在金融行业里当起了“破译者”。
cues.en: you started to become a code-cracker in the financial industry.

cues.zh: 我想你大概不认同有效市场理论。
cues.en: I think you probably didn't buy efficient market theory.

cues.zh: 不知怎的，你找到了在二十年间创造惊人回报的方法。
cues.en: Somehow you found a way of creating astonishing returns over two decades.

cues.zh: 别人向我解释的方式是，
cues.en: The way it's been explained to me,

cues.zh: 你所做之事了不起的地方不仅在于回报的规模，
cues.en: what's remarkable about what you did wasn't just the size of the returns,

cues.zh: 更在于你以出奇低的波动性和风险获得了这些回报，
cues.en: it's that you took them with surprisingly low volatility and risk,

cues.zh: 与其他对冲基金相比。
cues.en: compared with other hedge funds.

cues.zh: 那么你究竟是怎么做到的，Jim？
cues.en: So how on earth did you do this, Jim?

cues.zh: JS：我靠的是一群出色的人。
cues.en: JS: I did it by assembling a wonderful group of people.

cues.zh: 我开始做交易时，已经对数学有点厌倦了。
cues.en: When I started doing trading, I had gotten a little tired of mathematics.

cues.zh: 我当时快四十岁了，有点小钱。
cues.en: I was in my late 30s, I had a little money.

cues.zh: 我开始交易，进展非常顺利。
cues.en: I started trading and it went very well.

cues.zh: 我靠纯粹的运气赚了不少钱。
cues.en: I made quite a lot of money with pure luck.

cues.zh: 我是说，我觉得那纯粹是运气。
cues.en: I mean, I think it was pure luck.

cues.zh: 那肯定不是数学建模。
cues.en: It certainly wasn't mathematical modeling.

cues.zh: 但看了数据之后，过了一段时间我意识到：
cues.en: But in looking at the data, after a while I realized:

cues.zh: 这里似乎有一些结构。
cues.en: it looks like there's some structure here.

cues.zh: 于是我雇了几位数学家，开始建立一些模型——
cues.en: And I hired a few mathematicians, and we started making some models --

cues.zh: 就像我们在IDA（国防分析研究所）时做的那样。
cues.en: just the kind of thing we did back at IDA [Institute for Defense Analyses].

cues.zh: 你设计一个算法，在计算机上测试它。
cues.en: You design an algorithm, you test it out on a computer.

cues.zh: 它管用吗？不管用吗？诸如此类。
cues.en: Does it work? Doesn't it work? And so on.

cues.zh: CA：我们能看看这个吗？
cues.en: CA: Can we take a look at this?

cues.zh: 因为这是一张典型的大宗商品走势图。
cues.en: Because here's a typical graph of some commodity.

cues.zh: 我看着它说：“这不过是随机的上下波动——
cues.en: I look at that, and I say, "That's just a random, up-and-down walk --

cues.zh: 也许在整个时间段内有轻微的上升趋势。”
cues.en: maybe a slight upward trend over that whole period of time."

cues.zh: 你究竟怎么能看着这张图去做交易，
cues.en: How on earth could you trade looking at that,

cues.zh: 还能看出不是随机的东西？
cues.en: and see something that wasn't just random?

cues.zh: JS：过去——这是一张过去那种走势图，
cues.en: JS: In the old days -- this is kind of a graph from the old days,

cues.zh: 大宗商品或货币往往会有趋势。
cues.en: commodities or currencies had a tendency to trend.

cues.zh: 未必是你看到的这种极轻的趋势，而是按周期呈现的趋势。
cues.en: Not necessarily the very light trend you see here, but trending in periods.

cues.zh: 如果你决定，好，我要预测今天，
cues.en: And if you decided, OK, I'm going to predict today,

cues.zh: 用过去20天的平均走势——
cues.en: by the average move in the past 20 days --

cues.zh: 也许那会是个不错的预测，我还能赚点钱。
cues.en: maybe that would be a good prediction, and I'd make some money.

cues.zh: 事实上，多年前这样的系统会奏效——
cues.en: And in fact, years ago, such a system would work --

cues.zh: 不算漂亮，但确实管用。
cues.en: not beautifully, but it would work.

cues.zh: 你会赚钱，会亏钱，又会赚钱。
cues.en: You'd make money, you'd lose money, you'd make money.

cues.zh: 但这是一整年的天数，
cues.en: But this is a year's worth of days,

cues.zh: 在那段时间里你能赚一点钱。
cues.en: and you'd make a little money during that period.

cues.zh: 这是个非常退化的系统。
cues.en: It's a very vestigial system.

cues.zh: CA：所以你会测试各种时间长度的趋势
cues.en: CA: So you would test a bunch of lengths of trends in time

cues.zh: 看看比如
cues.en: and see whether, for example,

cues.zh: 10天趋势或15天趋势能否预测接下来发生的事。
cues.en: a 10-day trend or a 15-day trend was predictive of what happened next.

cues.zh: JS：当然，你会把这些都试一遍，看哪个效果最好。
cues.en: JS: Sure, you would try all those things and see what worked best.

cues.zh: 趋势跟踪在60年代会很有效，
cues.en: Trend-following would have been great in the '60s,

cues.zh: 在70年代还算可以。
cues.en: and it was sort of OK in the '70s.

cues.zh: 到了80年代，就不行了。
cues.en: By the '80s, it wasn't.

cues.zh: CA：因为所有人都能看出来了。
cues.en: CA: Because everyone could see that.

cues.en: So, how did you stay ahead of the pack?

cues.en: JS: We stayed ahead of the pack by finding other approaches --

cues.en: shorter-term approaches to some extent.

cues.zh: 真正关键的是收集大量数据——
cues.en: The real thing was to gather a tremendous amount of data --

cues.zh: 早期我们只能靠手工获取。
cues.en: and we had to get it by hand in the early days.

cues.en: We went down to the Federal Reserve and copied interest rate histories

cues.zh: 之类的东西，因为当时电脑里根本没有。
cues.en: and stuff like that, because it didn't exist on computers.

cues.zh: 我们搞到了大量数据。
cues.en: We got a lot of data.

cues.zh: 还有非常聪明的人——这才是关键。
cues.en: And very smart people -- that was the key.

cues.zh: 我其实不太懂怎么招人做基本面交易。
cues.en: I didn't really know how to hire people to do fundamental trading.

cues.zh: 我招了几个人——有的赚了钱，有的没赚。
cues.en: I had hired a few -- some made money, some didn't make money.

cues.zh: 我没能从中做出生意来。
cues.en: I couldn't make a business out of that.

cues.zh: 但我确实知道怎么招科学家，
cues.en: But I did know how to hire scientists,

cues.zh: 因为在这方面我还有点眼光。
cues.en: because I have some taste in that department.

cues.zh: 于是我们就这么做了。
cues.en: So, that's what we did.

cues.zh: 渐渐地，这些模型变得越来越好，
cues.en: And gradually these models got better and better,

cues.zh: 越来越好。
cues.en: and better and better.

cues.zh: CA：你在 Renaissance 做了一件了不起的事，
cues.en: CA: You're credited with doing something remarkable at Renaissance,

cues.zh: 就是打造了这种文化、这群人，
cues.en: which is building this culture, this group of people,

cues.zh: 他们不是那种能被钱挖走的雇佣兵。
cues.en: who weren't just hired guns who could be lured away by money.

cues.zh: 他们的动力是去做激动人心的数学和科学。
cues.en: Their motivation was doing exciting mathematics and science.

cues.zh: JS：嗯，我倒是希望确实如此。
cues.en: JS: Well, I'd hoped that might be true.

cues.zh: 但其中也有钱的因素。
cues.en: But some of it was money.

cues.en: CA: They made a lot of money.

cues.en: JS: I can't say that no one came because of the money.

cues.zh: 我觉得他们中很多人是因为钱来的。
cues.en: I think a lot of them came because of the money.

cues.en: But they also came because it would be fun.

cues.en: JS: In a certain sense, what we did was machine learning.

cues.zh: 你看大量数据，尝试模拟不同的预测方案，

cues.zh: 直到你越来越擅长这件事。
cues.en: until you get better and better at it.

cues.zh: 它不一定像我们那样自我反馈。
cues.en: It doesn't necessarily feed back on itself the way we did things.

cues.zh: 但它奏效了。
cues.en: But it worked.

cues.zh: CA：所以这些不同的预测方案可能相当疯狂和出人意料。
cues.en: CA: So these different predictive schemes can be really quite wild and unexpected.

cues.zh: 我是说，你什么都看了，对吧？
cues.en: I mean, you looked at everything, right?

cues.en: You looked at the weather, length of dresses, political opinion.

cues.zh: JS：是的，裙子长度我们没试。
cues.en: JS: Yes, length of dresses we didn't try.

cues.zh: CA：那都看些什么？
cues.en: CA: What sort of things?

cues.en: JS: Well, everything.

cues.en: Everything is grist for the mill -- except hem lengths.

cues.zh: 天气、年报、
cues.en: Weather, annual reports,

cues.en: quarterly reports, historic data itself, volumes, you name it.

cues.zh: 凡是有的都看。
cues.en: Whatever there is.

cues.zh: 我们每天摄入数TB的数据。
cues.en: We take in terabytes of data a day.

cues.zh: 把它存下来，整理加工，准备好做分析。
cues.en: And store it away and massage it and get it ready for analysis.

cues.zh: 你在寻找异常现象。
cues.en: You're looking for anomalies.

cues.zh: 你在寻找——就像你说的，
cues.en: You're looking for -- like you said,

cues.zh: 有效市场假说并不正确。
cues.en: the efficient market hypothesis is not correct.

cues.zh: CA：但任何一个异常现象都可能只是随机事件。
cues.en: CA: But any one anomaly might be just a random thing.

cues.zh: 那么，这里的秘诀是不是就是观察多个奇怪的异常现象，
cues.en: So, is the secret here to just look at multiple strange anomalies,

cues.zh: 看看它们何时相互吻合？
cues.en: and see when they align?

cues.zh: JS：任何一个异常现象都可能是随机事件；
cues.en: JS: Any one anomaly might be a random thing;

cues.zh: 不过，如果你有足够的数据，你就能判断出它不是。
cues.en: however, if you have enough data you can tell that it's not.

cues.zh: 你能看到一个异常现象持续足够长的时间——
cues.en: You can see an anomaly that's persistent for a sufficiently long time --

cues.zh: 它是随机出现的概率并不高。
cues.en: the probability of it being random is not high.

cues.zh: 但这些东西过一段时间就会消退；异常现象会被冲刷掉。
cues.en: But these things fade after a while; anomalies can get washed out.

cues.zh: 所以你必须时刻紧跟这个行业。
cues.en: So you have to keep on top of the business.

cues.en: CA: A lot of people look at the hedge fund industry now

cues.en: and how much talent is going into it.

cues.en: Do you have any worries about that industry,

cues.en: and perhaps the financial industry in general?

cues.zh: 就像是坐在一辆失控的列车上——
cues.en: Kind of being on a runaway train that's --

cues.zh: 怎么说呢——加剧了不平等？
cues.en: I don't know -- helping increase inequality?

cues.en: How would you champion what's happening in the hedge fund industry?

cues.en: JS: I think in the last three or four years,

cues.zh: 对冲基金的表现并不特别好。
cues.en: hedge funds have not done especially well.

cues.zh: 我们做得不错，
cues.en: We've done dandy,

cues.zh: 但整个对冲基金行业的表现没那么出色。
cues.en: but the hedge fund industry as a whole has not done so wonderfully.

cues.zh: 股市一路高歌猛进，大家都知道，
cues.en: The stock market has been on a roll, going up as everybody knows,

cues.zh: 市盈率也涨了。
cues.en: and price-earnings ratios have grown.

cues.zh: 所以过去——
cues.en: So an awful lot of the wealth that's been created in the last --

cues.en: let's say, five or six years -- has not been created by hedge funds.

cues.en: People would ask me, "What's a hedge fund?"

cues.zh: 我就说：“一和二十。”
cues.en: And I'd say, "One and 20."

cues.zh: 也就是说——现在是2和20——

cues.en: it's two percent fixed fee and 20 percent of profits.

cues.zh: 对冲基金是形形色色的物种。
cues.en: Hedge funds are all different kinds of creatures.

cues.en: CA: Five and 44.

cues.zh: 也就是5%的固定费用，44%的收益分成。

cues.en: You still made your investors spectacular amounts of money.

cues.zh: JS：是的，我们回报不错。
cues.en: JS: We made good returns, yes.

cues.en: People got very mad: "How can you charge such high fees?"

cues.en: I said, "OK, you can withdraw."

cues.zh: 但大家想的其实是“我怎么才能多投点”——
cues.en: But "How can I get more?" was what people were --

cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.en: CA: But should we worry about the hedge fund industry

cues.en: We hire astronomers and physicists and things like that.

cues.en: I don't think we should worry about it too much.

cues.en: It's still a pretty small industry.

cues.zh: 事实上，把科学引入投资界

cues.zh: 改善了这个世界。
cues.en: has improved that world.

cues.zh: 它降低了波动性，提高了流动性。
cues.en: It's reduced volatility. It's increased liquidity.

cues.zh: 价差变得更窄，因为人们在做这类交易。
cues.en: Spreads are narrower because people are trading that kind of stuff.

cues.zh: 所以我不太担心爱因斯坦跑去开对冲基金。
cues.en: So I'm not too worried about Einstein going off and starting a hedge fund.

cues.en: CA: You're at a phase in your life now where you're actually investing, though,

cues.en: at the other end of the supply chain --

cues.en: you're actually boosting mathematics across America.

cues.en: This is your wife, Marilyn.

cues.en: JS: Well, Marilyn started --

cues.en: she started the foundation about 20 years ago.

cues.en: I claim it was '93, she says it was '94,

cues.en: which was to focus on math and science, to focus on basic research.

cues.zh: 我们就是这么做的。
cues.en: And that's what we've done.

cues.zh: 这就是我们所做的事。

cues.en: giving them some extra income, giving them support and coaching.

cues.en: as part of a core.

cues.en: There's a great morale among them.

cues.en: They're staying in the field.

cues.zh: 我们这里看到的是什么？

cues.zh: 然后我再告诉你你看到的是什么。
cues.en: And then I'll tell you what you're looking at.

cues.en: Origins of life is a fascinating question.

cues.zh: 我们是怎么来的？
cues.en: How did we get here?

cues.zh: 这里有两个问题：
cues.en: Well, there are two questions:

cues.zh: 一个是，从地质到生物的路是怎么走的——
cues.en: One is, what is the route from geology to biology --

cues.zh: 我们是怎么来的？
cues.en: how did we get here?

cues.zh: 另一个问题是，我们一开始有什么？
cues.en: And the other question is, what did we start with?

cues.zh: 在这条路上，我们有什么材料可用，如果有的话？
cues.en: What material, if any, did we have to work with on this route?

cues.en: Those are two very, very interesting questions.

cues.en: The first question is a tortuous path from geology up to RNA

cues.zh: 或者类似的东西——这一切是怎么发生的？
cues.en: or something like that -- how did that all work?

cues.zh: 另一个是，我们有什么可用的？
cues.en: And the other, what do we have to work with?

cues.zh: 嗯，比我们想象的要多。
cues.en: Well, more than we think.

cues.zh: 所以那里画的是一个正在形成的恒星。
cues.en: So what's pictured there is a star in formation.

cues.zh: 每年，在我们这个有1000亿颗恒星的银河系里，
cues.en: Now, every year in our Milky Way, which has 100 billion stars,

cues.zh: 大约会诞生两颗新恒星。
cues.en: about two new stars are created.

cues.zh: 别问我怎么做到的，反正它们就是形成了。
cues.en: Don't ask me how, but they're created.

cues.zh: 它们大约要花一百万年才能稳定下来。
cues.en: And it takes them about a million years to settle out.

cues.zh: 所以，在稳定状态下，
cues.en: So, in steady state,

cues.zh: 任何时候都有大约两百万颗恒星正在形成。
cues.en: there are about two million stars in formation at any time.

cues.zh: 那一颗正处于这个稳定过程的某个阶段。
cues.en: That one is somewhere along this settling-down period.

cues.zh: 还有一堆乱七八糟的东西绕着它转，
cues.en: And there's all this crap sort of circling around it,

cues.zh: 尘埃之类的。
cues.en: dust and stuff.

cues.zh: 它大概会形成一个太阳系，或者形成别的什么。
cues.en: And it'll form probably a solar system, or whatever it forms.

cues.zh: 但关键在于——
cues.en: But here's the thing --

cues.zh: 在围绕形成中恒星的这片尘埃里
cues.en: in this dust that surrounds a forming star

cues.zh: 现在已经发现了重要的有机分子。
cues.en: have been found, now, significant organic molecules.

cues.zh: 不只是甲烷那样的分子，还有甲醛和氰化物——
cues.en: Molecules not just like methane, but formaldehyde and cyanide --

cues.zh: 这些是构建单元——可以说是生命的种子。
cues.en: things that are the building blocks -- the seeds, if you will -- of life.

cues.zh: 所以，那可能是普遍现象。
cues.en: So, that may be typical.

cues.zh: 也可能普遍的是，宇宙各处的行星
cues.en: And it may be typical that planets around the universe

cues.zh: 一开始就带着一些这样的基本构建单元。
cues.en: start off with some of these basic building blocks.

cues.zh: 那是否意味着生命会无处不在？
cues.en: Now does that mean there's going to be life all around?

cues.zh: 也许吧。
cues.en: Maybe.

cues.zh: 但问题在于这条路有多曲折，
cues.en: But it's a question of how tortuous this path is

cues.zh: 从那些脆弱的开端、那些种子，一路走到生命。
cues.en: from those frail beginnings, those seeds, all the way to life.

cues.zh: 而大多数种子会落在荒芜的行星上。
cues.en: And most of those seeds will fall on fallow planets.

cues.zh: CA：那么对你个人而言，
cues.en: CA: So for you, personally,

cues.zh: 找到我们来自何处这个问题的答案，
cues.en: finding an answer to this question of where we came from,

cues.zh: 弄清楚这件事是如何发生的，是你很想看到的。
cues.en: of how did this thing happen, that is something you would love to see.

cues.zh: JS：很想看到。
cues.en: JS: Would love to see.

cues.zh: 也想知道——
cues.en: And like to know --

cues.zh: 如果这条路足够曲折、足够不可能，
cues.en: if that path is tortuous enough, and so improbable,

cues.zh: 那么无论从什么起点出发，我们都可能是独一无二的。
cues.en: that no matter what you start with, we could be a singularity.

cues.zh: 但另一方面，
cues.en: But on the other hand,

cues.zh: 考虑到周围漂浮着这么多有机尘埃，
cues.en: given all this organic dust that's floating around,

cues.zh: 我们外面可能有很多朋友。
cues.en: we could have lots of friends out there.

cues.zh: 知道这一点会很棒。
cues.en: It'd be great to know.

cues.zh: CA：Jim，几年前我有机会和Elon Musk交谈，
cues.en: CA: Jim, a couple of years ago, I got the chance to speak with Elon Musk,

cues.zh: 我问了他成功的秘诀，
cues.en: and I asked him the secret of his success,

cues.zh: 他说认真对待物理学就是秘诀。
cues.en: and he said taking physics seriously was it.

cues.zh: 听你这么说，我听到的是认真对待数学，
cues.en: Listening to you, what I hear you saying is taking math seriously,

cues.zh: 这已经融入了你的一生。
cues.en: that has infused your whole life.

cues.zh: 它让你赚了巨额财富，现在又让你能够投资
cues.en: It's made you an absolute fortune, and now it's allowing you to invest

cues.zh: 于美国乃至其他地方成千上万孩子的未来。
cues.en: in the futures of thousands and thousands of kids across America and elsewhere.

cues.zh: 难道说科学真的管用？
cues.en: Could it be that science actually works?

cues.zh: 数学真的管用？
cues.en: That math actually works?

cues.zh: JS：嗯，数学当然管用。数学当然管用。
cues.en: JS: Well, math certainly works. Math certainly works.

cues.zh: 但这一路很有趣。
cues.en: But this has been fun.

cues.zh: 和 Marilyn 一起合作并把它捐出去，非常令人愉快。
cues.en: Working with Marilyn and giving it away has been very enjoyable.

cues.zh: CA：我只是觉得——这对我来说是个鼓舞人心的想法，
cues.en: CA: I just find it -- it's an inspirational thought to me,

cues.zh: 认真对待知识，就能从中收获更多。
cues.en: that by taking knowledge seriously, so much more can come from it.

cues.zh: 所以感谢你精彩的一生，也感谢你来到 TED。
cues.en: So thank you for your amazing life, and for coming here to TED.

cues.zh: 谢谢。
cues.en: Thank you.

cues.zh: Jim Simons！
cues.en: Jim Simons!

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
